title: Declarative cohort similarity routing and graceful canary drain for staged model rollouts
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds cohort-aware similarity routing to improve canary drains and reduce tail-latency regressions. Backwards compatible and feature-gated.
commits: controller: add CohortSimilarityRouter and lifecycle state machine
runtime: fast fingerprint index and LRU-backed similarity cache
tests: unit and integration tests for drain scenarios
ci: tighten lint and add integration workflow for rollout_e2e
description:
Context: We have observed tail-latency spikes and cache pollution during canary drains for models that diverge behaviorally from the primary model. Existing time-windowed drains and traffic-splitting strategies either hold back traffic for too long or abruptly shift traffic causing downstream SLO regressions. This PR introduces a declarative, cohort-aware similarity routing layer that gracefully drains canaries by steering requests based on request-to-model similarity fingerprints.

Summary: Adds a CohortSimilarityRouter to the rollout controller which computes a lightweight fingerprint per request and routes cohorts to model variants according to an operator-specified similarity threshold. The rollout spec (api/schemas/rollout_v2.yaml) includes cohortRules and similarityThresholds that let teams express: targeted A/B splits by cohort, speculative routing for ambiguous requests (dual-call + winner-take-all), and a staged drain that reduces traffic to the canary only for high-similarity cohorts first. The runtime component uses an LRU-backed similarity cache and a compact locality-sensitive hashing index for O(1) approximate similarity checks, minimizing per-request overhead.

Checklist: 
- [x] design doc and prototype spike validated with load tests (see docs/rollouts/cohort_similarity_routing.md)
- [x] rollout API extension and backwards-compatible parsing
- [x] runtime similarity index with micro-benchmarks
- [x] integration tests for drain scenarios and A/B cohorts
- [x] observability: rollout metrics and tracing for similarity decisions
- [x] feature-flag gated rollout (off by default)

Key behaviors and safety: The router is opt-in per rollout and can be enabled only for rosters that opt into cohort routing. Drain progresses in three deterministic stages: (1) similarity-first reduction where only high-similarity cohorts are shifted to canary, (2) progressive blending where threshold relaxes, and (3) full swap. At any stage, if SLO gates in the Console are breached (latency or quality regressions), an automated rollback playback is triggered that replays a bounded sample of requests against the previous model for root-cause collection and then performs an immediate traffic revert. The playback is stored in the rollout journal for auditing.

Performance: Microbenchmarks on c6g-like instances show median per-request overhead of ~0.8ms for the similarity check when the index is warm; end-to-end 95th latency impact across a mixed workload was <2% for 99th token latency. Load test details and artifact links included in the design doc.

Testing and QA: New unit tests cover the similarity index edge cases and hash collisions. Integration e2e uses ci/workflows/rollout_e2e.yml to validate a staged drain under synthetic cohorts; tests simulate SLO regression to verify automated rollback sequence. Manual verification steps are documented under docs/rollouts/cohort_similarity_routing.md.

Files changed at a glance: 
- services/rollout/controller.py: adds CohortSimilarityRouter, new lifecycle states (SIMILARITY_DRAINING, BLEND), and handlers for automated rollback playback.
- services/rollout/similarity_index.py: LSH-based index plus LRU cache and async warming logic.
- services/rollout/drain_policy.py: declarative drain planner implementing the three-stage drain.
- api/schemas/rollout_v2.yaml: rollout spec extension with examples in examples/rollouts/cohort_similarity_example.yaml.
- docs/rollouts/cohort_similarity_routing.md: design rationale, ops runbook, and rollback playbook.

Review thread (high-level): 
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Strong design; two requests: add an integration test that simulates cache cold starts, and ensure the similarity decision is logged at debug level only behind a flag." 
- Maya Chen (author): "Addressed: added test for cold start in test_cohort_routing.py and gated verbose logging behind TRACE_SIMILARITY flag; pushed new commits." 
- Sofia Martinez (reviewer): "Can you quantify memory footprint for the LRU cache under typical rollout sizes? Recommend a telemetry gauge." 
- Maya Chen: "Added telemetry gauge (rollout_similarity_cache_size) and documented sizing guidance in observability/metrics/rollout_metrics.md." 
- Ethan Green: "Approvals aside from minor nits in naming—suggest squash on merge to keep history small."

CI summary: rollout_e2e (passed), unit (passed), lint (passed after fix), integration (passed). One flaky test (tests/rollouts/test_cohort_routing.py::test_blend_transition) failed initially on CI due to timing assumptions; adjusted to wait for consistency and retried successfully.

Merge: Squash merge into main performed on 2026-02-24 by Maya Chen. Merge commit message notes ENG-11234 and includes brief rollout enabling steps.

Post-merge rollout notes: The feature is feature-flag gated; recommended rollout plan for customers: enable on canary selection only with conservative similarity thresholds (0.9) and monitor the new metrics rollout_similarity_decisions_total and rollout_similarity_cache_size for 48 hours before relaxing thresholds. Run the provided migration job to warm indices for historical cohorts if enabling on long-lived traffic rosters.

Related work: This PR complements previous staged rollout controllers by adding content-aware routing and deterministic drains; it intentionally avoids altering the core fallback routing logic and instead plugs into the existing decision pipeline.
notes: Ops runbook and rollback playbook added
